p2.original: The Increasing Value of a College Degree
p2.zh: 学院学位的不断提高的价值

p3.original: Working your way through college used to be fairly common in the United States. According to a 2015 study by the Georgetown Center on Education and the Workforce, 40% of college students work 30 hours or more per week.
p3.zh: 在美国很常见的大学里工作 根据乔治城教育和劳动力中心2015年的一项研究,40%的大学生每周工作30小时或以上.

p4.original: At the same time, the cost of college seems to rise every year. The data show that between the 2000–2001 academic year and the 2019–2020 academic year, the cost of tuition, fees, and room and board has slightly more than doubled for private four-year colleges, and has increased by a factor of almost 2.5 for public four-year colleges. Thus, even full time employment may not be enough to cover college expenses anymore.  Working full time at minimum wage—40 hours per week, 52 weeks per year—earns $15,080 before taxes, which is substantially less than the more than $25,000 estimated as the average cost in 2022 for a year of college at a public university.  The result of these costs is that student loan debt topped $1.3 trillion this year.
p4.zh: 同时,大学的费用似乎每年都在上升.数据显示,2000–2001学年至2019–2020学年,私立四年制学院的学费,学费,食宿费略微翻了一番以上,公立四年制学院的学费增长了近2.5倍. 因此,即使全职工作也可能不足以支付大学费用。每周40小时、每年52周的全日工作,在纳税前为15 080美元,大大低于2022年公立大学一年大学平均费用估计的25,000美元。这些费用的结果是今年学生贷款债务高达1.3万亿美元。

p5.original: Despite these disheartening figures, the value of a bachelor’s degree has never been higher.   How do we explain this?  This chapter will tell us.
p5.zh: 尽管有这些令人沮丧的数字,但学士学位的价值从未如此高过。 我们如何解释?本章将告诉我们。

p14.original:
In a market economy like the United States, income comes from ownership of the means of production: resources or assets.  More precisely, one’s income is a function of two things:   the quantity of each resource one owns, and the value society places on those resources.
Recall from the chapter on Production, Costs, and Industry Structure, each factor of production has an associated factor payment.  For the majority of us, the most important resource we own is our labor.  Thus, most of our income is wages, salaries, commissions, tips and other types of labor income. Your labor income depends on how many hours you work and the wage rate an employer will pay you for those hours.  At the same time, some people own real estate, which they can either use themselves or rent out to other users.  Some people have financial assets like bank accounts, stocks and bonds, for which they earn interest, dividends or some other form of income.
p14.zh: 在美国这样的市场经济中,收入来自生产资料的所有权:资源或资产.更确切地说,一个人的收入由两件事来决定:一个人拥有的每一种资源的数量,以及社会对这些资源的价值。 从关于生产、成本和工业结构的一章中回顾,每个生产要素都有相关的要素付款。对我们大多数人来说,我们拥有的最重要资源就是我们的劳动。 因此,我们的大部分收入是工资、工资、佣金、小费和其他类型的劳动收入。 您的劳动收入取决于您工作的时间和工资标准,雇主会为您支付这些时间的工资。 同时,有些人拥有房地产,他们可以自己使用,也可以租给其他用户.一些人拥有银行账户,股票和债券等金融资产,为此他们赚取利息,股利或者某种其他形式的收入.

p15.original: Each of these factor payments, like wages for labor and interest for financial capital, is determined in their respective factor markets.  For the rest of this chapter, we will focus on labor markets, but other factor markets operate similarly.  Later in Chapter 17 we will describe how this works for financial capital.
p15.zh: 这些要素付款,如劳动力工资和金融资本利息,都由各自的要素市场决定。 在本章的其余部分,我们将侧重于劳动力市场,但其他因素市场的运作类似。 在第17章的后面,我们将描述这如何为金融资本发挥作用。

p18.original: The labor market is the term that economists use for all the different markets for labor.  There is no single labor market.  Rather, there is a different market for every different type of labor.  Labor differs by type of work (e.g. retail sales vs. scientist), skill level (entry level or more experienced), and location (the market for administrative assistants is probably more local or regional than the market for university presidents).  While each labor market is different, they all tend to operate in similar ways.  For example, when wages go up in one labor market, they tend to go up in others too.  When economists talk about the labor market, they are describing these similarities.
p18.zh: 劳动力市场是经济学家对所有不同劳动力市场使用的术语。没有一个单一的劳动力市场。 相反,每种不同类型的劳动力都有不同的市场。劳动因工作类型(如零售对科学家),技能水平(入职水平或经验更丰富)和地点(行政助理的市场可能比大学校长的市场更本地或地区)而异. 虽然每个劳动力市场都不同,但它们都倾向于以类似方式运作。 例如,当工资在一个劳动力市场上升时,在其他劳动力市场也往往上升。 当经济学家谈论劳动力市场时,他们正在描述这些相似之处。

p19.original: The labor market, like all markets, has a demand and a supply.  Why do firms demand labor?  Why is an employer willing to pay you for your labor?  It’s not because the employer likes you or is socially conscious.  Rather, it’s because your labor is worth something to the employer--your work brings in revenues to the firm.  How much is an employer willing to pay?  That depends on the skills and experience you bring to the firm.
p19.zh: 劳动力市场与所有市场一样,有需求和供应。企业为什么需要劳动力? 为什么雇主愿意付你劳动费? 不是因为雇主喜欢你, 而是因为你的劳动对雇主来说是值得的, 你的工作为公司带来收入。雇主愿意付多少钱? 这取决于你给公司带来的技能和经验。

p20.original: If a firm wants to maximize profits, it will never pay more (in terms of wages and benefits) for a worker than the value of their marginal productivity to the firm.  We call this the first rule of labor markets.
p20.zh: 如果公司想要实现利润最大化,它为工人支付的报酬(在工资和福利方面)永远不会超过他们向公司支付的边际生产力的价值。 我们称之为劳动力市场的第一条规则。

p21.original: Suppose a worker can produce two widgets per hour and the firm can sell each widget for $4 each.  Then the worker is generating $8 per hour in revenues to the firm, and a profit-maximizing employer will pay the worker up to, but no more than, $8 per hour, because that is what the worker is worth to the firm.
p21.zh: 假设一个工人可以每小时生产两个部件,公司可以每个部件售出4美元. 然后,工人每小时向公司赚取8美元的收入,一个利润最大化的雇主将向工人支付每小时8美元,但不超过8美元,因为这是工人对公司的价值。

p22.original: Recall the definition of marginal product.  Marginal product is the additional output a firm can produce by adding one more worker to the production process.  Since employers often hire labor by the hour, we’ll define marginal product as the additional output the firm produces by adding one more worker hour to the production process.  In this chapter, we assume that workers in a particular labor market are homogeneous—they have the same background, experience and skills and they put in the same amount of effort.  Thus, marginal product depends on the capital and technology with which workers have to work.
p22.zh: 回顾边际产品的定义.边际产品是一家企业通过在生产过程中再增加一名工人而能够产生的额外产出. 因为雇主常常在一小时前雇佣劳工, 我们将把边际产品定义为企业生产的额外产出, 在本章中,我们假定某一劳动力市场上的工人是同质的——他们具有同样的背景、经验和技能,他们付出了同样的努力。 因此,边际产品取决于工人必须与之合作的资本和技术。

p23.original: A typist can type more pages per hour with an electric typewriter than a manual typewriter, and the typist can type even more pages per hour with a personal computer and word processing software.  A ditch digger can dig more cubic feet of dirt in an hour with a backhoe than with a shovel.
p23.zh: 一个打字员可以用电打字机每小时打出更多的页面,比手动打字机还要多,打字员可以用个人电脑和文字处理软件每小时打出更多的页面.挖沟者在一个小时内可以挖出更多立方英尺的土,用回蹄,比用铲子挖得还要多.

p24.original: Thus, we can define the demand for labor as the marginal product of labor times the value of that output to the firm.
p24.zh: 因此,我们可以把对劳动力的需求定义为劳动力的边际产品,其时间是该产出对企业的价值。

p63.original: Demand for Labor in Perfectly Competitive Output Markets
p63.zh: 完全竞争性产出市场对劳动力的需求

p64.original: The question for any firm is how much labor to hire.
p64.zh: 任何公司都得考虑 雇用多少劳动力

p65.original: We can define a Perfectly Competitive Labor Market as one where firms can hire all the labor they want at the going market wage.  Think about secretaries in a large city.  Employers who need secretaries can probably hire as many as they need if they pay the going wage rate.
p65.zh: 我们可以将一个完全有竞争力的劳动力市场定义为一个企业能够雇佣所有他们想要的劳动力的市场工资。想想大城市的秘书们需要秘书的雇主如果支付持续工资率,可以雇用尽可能多的人。

p70.original: Economists describe the demand for inputs like labor as a derived demand.   Since the demand for labor is MPL*P, it is dependent on the demand for the product the firm is producing.  We show this by the P term in the demand for labor.  An increase in demand for the firm’s product drives up the product’s price, which increases the firm’s demand for labor.  Thus, we derive the demand for labor from the demand for the firm’s output.
p70.zh: 经济学家将对劳动力等投入的需求描述为衍生需求. 由于对劳动力的需求是MPL*P,它取决于对企业正在生产的产品的需求。 我们用P这个词来说明对劳动力的需求。 对公司产品需求的增加促使产品价格上升,从而增加了公司对劳动力的需求。 因此,我们对劳动力的需求来自对公司产出的需求。

p71.original: Demand for Labor in Imperfectly Competitive Output Markets
p71.zh: 缺乏竞争力的产出市场对劳动力的需求

p72.original: If the employer does not sell its output in a perfectly competitive industry, they face a downward sloping demand curve for output, which means that in order to sell additional output the firm must lower its price.  This is true if the firm is a monopoly, but it’s also true if the firm is an oligopoly or monopolistically competitive.  In this situation, the value of a worker’s marginal product is the marginal revenue, not the price.  Thus, the demand for labor is the marginal product times the marginal revenue.
p72.zh: 如果雇主不在一个完全有竞争力的行业中出售其产出,他们就会面临产出需求下滑的曲线,这意味着为了出售额外产出,公司必须降低价格。 如果公司是垄断公司,这是事实,但如果公司是寡头垄断或垄断竞争,也是事实。 在这种情况下,工人的边际产品的价值是边际收入,而不是价格。 因此,对劳动力的需求是边际产品乘以边际收入。

p73.original: The Demand for Labor = MPL x MR = Marginal Revenue Product
p73.zh: 劳动力需求=MPLxMR=边际收入产品

p98.original: Do Profit Maximizing Employers Exploit Labor?
p98.zh: 是否使雇主剥削劳工获得最大利润?

p99.original: If you look back at , you will see that the firm pays only the last worker it hires what they’re worth to the firm.  Every other worker brings in more revenue than the firm pays them.  This has sometimes led to the claim that employers exploit workers because they do not pay workers what they are worth.  Let’s think about this claim.   The first worker is worth $x to the firm, and the second worker is worth $y, but why are they worth that much?  It is because of the capital and technology with which they work.  The difference between workers’ worth and their compensation goes to pay for the capital and technology, without which the workers wouldn’t have a job.  The difference also goes to the employer’s profit, without which the firm would close and workers wouldn’t have a job.  The firm may be earning excessive profits, but that is a different topic of discussion.
p99.zh: 如果你回头看,你会看到公司只支付它雇用的最后一名工人对公司的价值。所有其他工人的收入都比公司付给他们的收入要多。 这有时导致有人声称雇主剥削工人,因为他们不向工人支付他们应得的报酬。 让我们想想这个说法。 第一个工人对公司来说是值$x的,第二个工人是值$y的,但为什么他们值这么多?这是因为他们工作时所借助的资本和技术。工人的价值和报酬之间的差别在于支付资本和技术,没有资本和技术,工人就没有工作。雇主的利润也存在差别,没有利润,公司就会关闭,工人就不会有工作。公司可能利润过高,但这是讨论的另一个话题。

p100.original: What Determines the Going Market Wage Rate?
p100.zh: 市场工资率是怎样决定的?

p101.original: In the chapter on Labor and Financial Markets, we learned that the labor market has demand and supply curves like other markets.  The demand for labor curve is a downward sloping function of the wage rate.  The market demand for labor is the horizontal sum of all firms’ demands for labor.  The supply of labor curve is an upward sloping function of the wage rate.  This is because if wages for a particular type of labor increase in a particular labor market, people with appropriate skills may change jobs, and vacancies will attract people from outside the geographic area.  The market supply of labor is the horizontal summation of all individuals’ supplies of labor.
p101.zh: 在关于劳动和金融市场的一章中,我们了解到,劳动力市场与其他市场一样,有供求曲线。劳动力需求曲线是工资率的下斜函数。市场对劳动力的需求是所有企业对劳动力的需求的横向总和。劳动力供应曲线是工资率的上升函数。这是因为,如果某一劳动力市场某类劳动力的工资增加,具有适当技能的人可能改变工作,空缺将吸引来自地理区域以外的人。劳动力的市场供应是所有个人劳动力供应的横向总和。

p103.original: Like all equilibrium prices, the market wage rate is determined through the interaction of supply and demand in the labor market.  Thus, we can see in  for competitive markets the wage rate and number of workers hired.
p103.zh: 与所有均衡价格一样,市场工资率是通过劳动力市场供求互动来确定的。 这样,我们就可以看到竞争性市场的工资率和雇用的工人人数。

p109.original: A firm demands labor because of the value of the labor’s marginal productivity.  For a firm operating in a perfectly competitive output market, this will be the value of the marginal product, which we define as the marginal product of labor multiplied by the firm’s output price.  For a firm which is not perfectly competitive, the appropriate concept is the marginal revenue product, which we define as the marginal product of labor multiplied by the firm’s marginal revenue.  Profit maximizing firms employ labor up to the point where the market wage is equal to the firm’s demand for labor.  In a competitive labor market, we determine market wage  through the interaction between the market supply and market demand for labor.
p109.zh: 企业要求劳动力,因为劳动力的边际生产力的价值。 对于在完全竞争性产出市场上经营的公司来说,这将是边际产品的价值,我们将其定义为劳动力边际产品乘以公司的产出价格。 对于一个没有完全竞争力的公司来说,适当的概念是边际收入产品,我们将其定义为劳动力的边际产品乘以公司的边际收入。利润最大化的企业雇用劳动力,直到市场工资与企业对劳动力的需求相等。 在竞争性劳动力市场中,我们通过市场供应和市场对劳动力的需求之间的相互作用来确定市场工资。

p122.original: Do unions typically oppose new technology out of a fear that it will reduce the number of union jobs? Why or why not?
p122.zh: 工会通常反对新技术,因为担心新技术会减少工会工作? 为什么或为什么不呢?

p123.original: Unions have sometimes opposed new technology out of a fear of losing jobs, but in other cases unions have helped to facilitate the introduction of new technology because unionized workers felt that the union was looking after their interests or that their higher skills meant that their jobs were essentially protected. And the new technologies meant increased productivity.
p123.zh: 工会有时出于对失去工作的恐惧而反对新技术,但在其他情况下,工会帮助促进新技术的引进,因为工会工人认为工会在照顾他们的利益,或者他们的更高技能意味着他们的工作基本上受到保护.新技术意味着生产力的提高。

p124.original: Compared with the share of workers in most other high-income countries, is the share of U.S. workers whose wages are determined by union bargaining higher or lower? Why or why not?

p125.original: In a few other countries (such as France and Spain), the percentage of workers belonging to a union is similar to that in the United States. When the share of workers whose wages are determined by union negotiations is considered, the United States ranks by far the lowest (because in countries like France and Spain, union negotiations often determine pay even for nonunion employees).
p125.zh: 在少数其他国家(如法国和西班牙),加入工会的工人比例与美国相似. 然而,美国加入联盟的比率普遍较低。 在考虑工资由工会谈判决定的工人比例时,美国排名远远低于最低(因为在法国和西班牙等国家,工会谈判往往甚至决定非工会雇员的工资).

p126.original: Are firms with a high percentage of union employees more likely to go bankrupt because of the higher wages that they pay? Why or why not?
p126.zh: 工会雇员比例较高的公司是否因为工资较高而更可能破产? 为什么或为什么不呢?

p127.original: No. While some unions may cause firms to go bankrupt, other unions help firms to become more competitive. No overall pattern exists.
p127.zh: 没有。 虽然有些工会可能使公司破产,但其他工会则帮助公司提高竞争力。不存在总体模式。

p129.original: From a social point of view, the benefits of unions and the costs seem to counterbalance. There is no evidence that in countries with a higher percentage of unionized workers, the economies grow more or less slowly.
p129.zh: 从社会角度看,工会的好处和代价似乎可以抵消。没有任何证据表明,在工会工人比例较高的国家,经济的增长或多或少缓慢。

p151.original: In the chapters on market structure, we observed that while economists use the theory of perfect competition as an ideal case of market structure, there are very few examples of perfectly competitive industries in the real world.  What about labor markets?  How many labor markets are perfectly competitive?  There are probably more examples of perfectly competitive labor markets than perfectly competitive product markets, but that doesn’t mean that all labor markets are competitive.
p151.zh: 在关于市场结构的章节中,我们观察到,虽然经济学家将完美竞争理论作为市场结构的理想案例,但现实世界中完全竞争的产业的例子却很少.劳动力市场怎么办?有多少劳动力市场是完全具有竞争力的? 但这并不表示所有劳动力市场都具有竞争力。

p152.original: When a job applicant is bargaining with an employer for a position, the applicant is often at a disadvantage—needing the job more than the employer needs that particular applicant. John Bates Clark (1847–1938), often named as the first great American economist, wrote in 1907: “In the making of the wages contract the individual laborer is always at a disadvantage. He has something which he is obliged to sell and which his employer is not obliged to take, since he [that is, the employer] can reject single men with impunity.”
p152.zh: 当求职者与雇主谈判争取职位时,申请者往往处于劣势——比雇主更需要该职位。 约翰·贝茨·克拉克(1847年–1938年)常被命名为美国第一位伟大的经济学家,1907年写道:"在工资合同的订立中,个体劳工总是处于劣势. 他有他必须出售的东西,他的雇主没有义务拿走,因为他[即雇主]可以拒绝单身男子而不受惩罚。”

These are demand side sources, that is, labor market power by employers, and supply side sources: labor market power by employees.  In this section we will discuss the former.  In the next section we will discuss the latter.
p195.zh: 劳动力市场的竞争不完善有两个来源。 这些是需求方来源,即雇主的劳动力市场实力,以及供应方来源:雇员的劳动力市场实力。 在本节中,我们将讨论前者。 在下一节,我们将讨论后者。

p196.original: A competitive labor market is one where there are many potential employers for a given type of worker, say a secretary or an accountant. Suppose there is only one employer in a labor market.  Because that employer has no direct competition in hiring, if they offer lower wages than would exist in a competitive market, employees will have few options.  If they want a job, they must accept the offered wage rate.  Since the employer is exploiting its market power, we call the firm a monopsony, a term introduced and widely discussed by Joan Robinson (though she credited scholar Bertrand Hallward with invention of the word). The classical example of monopsony is the sole coal company in a West Virginia town.  If coal miners want to work, they must accept what the coal company is paying.  This is not the only example of monopsony. Think about surgical nurses in a town with only one hospital.  A situation in which employers have at least some market power over potential employees is not that unusual.  After all, most firms have many employees while there is only one employer. Thus, even if there is some competition for workers, it may not feel that way to potential employees unless they do their research and find the opposite.
p196.zh: 竞争性的劳动力市场是存在许多潜在雇主,例如秘书或会计师的某一类工人。假设劳动力市场上只有一个雇主。 由于雇主在雇用方面没有直接的竞争,如果他们提供的工资低于在竞争性市场上存在的工资,雇员将几乎没有选择。 如果他们想要工作,他们必须接受提供的工资标准。 由于雇主正在利用其市场力量,我们称公司为单词,这个术语由Joan Robinson提出并广泛讨论(尽管她以这个词的发明来表扬学者Bertrand Hallward).典型的独占式的例子,是西弗吉尼亚州的一个城镇中唯一的煤炭公司. 如果煤矿工人想工作,他们必须接受煤炭公司支付的费用. 这不是单调的唯一例子。 想一想在只有一个医院的镇上做手术护士.雇主至少对潜在雇员拥有一定的市场支配力的情况并不罕见。毕竟,大多数公司有许多雇员,而只有一个雇主。 因此,即使对工人有某种竞争,除非潜在雇员进行研究并发现相反的情况,否则他们可能不会有这种感觉。

p197.original: How does market power by an employer affect labor market outcomes?  Intuitively, one might think that wages will be lower than in a competitive labor market.  Let’s prove it.  We will tell the story for a monopsonist, but the results will be qualitatively similar, although less extreme, for any firm with labor market power.
p197.zh: 雇主的市场力量如何影响劳动力市场的结果?直觉上,人们可能认为工资将低于竞争性劳动力市场。 让我们证明一下。 我们将为一位垄断主义者讲述这个故事,但对于任何拥有劳动力市场实力的公司来说,结果在质量上是相似的,尽管不那么极端。

p198.original: Think back to monopoly.  The good news for the firm is that because the monopolist is the sole supplier in the market, it can charge any price it wishes.  The bad news is that if it wants to sell a greater quantity of output, it must lower the price it charges.  Monopsony is analogous.  Because the monopsonist is the sole employer in a labor market, it can offer any wage that it wishes.  However, because they face the market supply curve for labor, if they want to hire more workers, they must raise the wage they pay.  This creates a quandary, which we can understand by introducing a new concept: the marginal cost of labor.   The marginal cost of labor is the cost to the firm of hiring one more worker.  However, here is the thing: we assume that the firm is determining how many workers to hire in total.  They are not hiring sequentially.  Let’s look how this plays out with the example in .
p198.zh: 回想垄断。公司的一个好消息是,由于垄断者是市场上唯一的供应商,它可以收取任何它想要的价格.坏消息是,如果它想出售更多的产出,就必须降低它收取的价格. 莫诺普索尼是相似的。 由于垄断者是劳动力市场上唯一的雇主,因此它可以提供它希望的任何工资。 然而,由于他们面临劳动力的市场供应曲线,如果他们想要雇用更多的工人,他们必须提高工资. 这造成了一个难题,我们可以通过引入一个新概念来理解:劳动力的边际成本。劳动力的边际成本是企业再雇用一名工人的成本。 然而,问题是:我们假设,公司正在决定总共雇用多少工人。 他们不是按顺序雇用的。 让我们看看这个例子是如何表现的。

p224.original: There are a couple of things to notice from the table.  First, the marginal cost increases faster than the wage rate.  In fact, for any number of workers more than one, the marginal cost of labor is greater than the wage.  This is because to hire one more worker requires paying a higher wage rate, not just for the new worker but for all the previous hires also.  We can see this graphically in Figure 14.7.
p224.zh: 桌子上有几件东西要注意 首先,边际成本的增长速度比工资率快。 事实上,对于任何数量以上的工人来说,劳动的边际成本比工资还要高.这是因为要再雇用一名工人,就必须支付更高的工资,不仅为新工人,而且为以前所有雇员支付更高的工资。 我们从图14.7中可以看出这一点。

p226.zh: 垄断下的劳动力市场结果

p227.original: If the firm wants to maximize profits, it will hire labor up to the point Lm where DL = VMP (or MRP) = MCL, as  shows.  Then, the supply curve for labor shows the wage the firm will have to pay to attract Lm workers.   Graphically, we can draw a vertical line up from Lm to the Supply Curve for the label and then read the wage Wm off the vertical axis to the left.
p227.zh: 如果公司想获得最大利润,它将雇用劳动力,直至DL=VMP(或MRP)=MCL(如所示)。接下来,劳动力的供应曲线显示,企业必须支付的工资吸引Lm工人. 从图形上,我们可以绘制一条从Lm到供给曲线的垂直线条来表示标签,然后从垂直轴向左读取工资Wm.

p228.original: How does this outcome compare to what would occur in a perfectly competitive market?  A competitive market would operate where DL = SL, hiring Lc workers and paying Wc wage.  In other words, under monopsony employers hire fewer workers and pay a lower wage.  While pure monopsony may be rare, many employers have some degree of market power in labor markets.  The outcomes for those employers will be qualitatively similar though not as extreme as monopsony.
p228.zh: 这一结果如何与在竞争激烈的市场中会发生的情况相比较?竞争性市场将在DL=SL、雇用Lc工人和支付Wc工资的情况下运作。换句话说,雇主在垄断下雇用的工人较少,工资较低。 虽然纯粹的垄断行为可能很少见,但许多雇主在劳动力市场上拥有一定程度的市场支配力。 这些雇主的结果在质量上是相似的,但不像独占式那样极端。

p229.original: Comparison of labor market outcomes: Monopsony vs. Perfect Competition
p229.zh: 劳动力市场结果比较:Monopsony vs.完美的竞争

p231.original: A monopsony is the sole employer in a labor market.  The monopsony can pay any wage it chooses, subject to the market supply of labor.  This means that if the monopsony offers too low a wage, they may not find enough workers willing to work for them.  Since to obtain more workers, they must offer a higher wage, the marginal cost of additional labor is greater than the wage.  To maximize profits, a monopsonist will hire workers up to the point where the marginal cost of labor equals their labor demand.  This results in a lower level of employment than a competitive labor market would provide, but also a lower equilibrium wage.
p231.zh: 垄断是劳动力市场上唯一的雇主。垄断者可以支付其选择的任何工资,但取决于劳力的市场供应情况。 这意味着,如果单币工资太低,他们可能找不到足够的工人愿意为他们工作。 由于要获得更多的工人,他们必须提供更高的工资,额外劳动力的边际成本要高于工资. 为了实现利润最大化,一个垄断主义者将雇用工人,直到劳动力的边际成本等于他们的劳动力需求。 这导致就业水平低于竞争性劳动力市场提供的水平,但也导致工资平衡水平降低。

p233.original: What is the marginal cost of labor for a firm that operates in a competitive labor market?  How does this compare with the MCL for a monopsony?
p233.zh: 在竞争性劳动力市场上经营的公司,劳动力的边际成本是什么? 这和监控罪有关吗?

p239.original: Market Power on the Supply Side of Labor Markets: Unions
p239.zh: 劳动力市场供应方面的市场力量:工会

p240.original: A labor union is an organization of workers that negotiates with employers over wages and working conditions. A labor union seeks to change the balance of power between employers and workers by requiring employers to deal with workers collectively, rather than as individuals.  As such, a labor union operates like a monopoly in a labor market.  We sometimes call negotiations between unions and firms collective bargaining.
p240.zh: 工会是一个工人组织,与雇主就工资和工作条件进行谈判。工会寻求改变雇主和工人之间的权力平衡,要求雇主集体而不是作为个人对待工人。 因此,工会在劳动力市场上的运作就像垄断。 我们有时要求工会和公司之间进行谈判,进行集体谈判。

p241.original: The subject of labor unions can be controversial. Supporters of labor unions view them as the workers’ primary line of defense against efforts by profit-seeking firms to hold down wages and benefits. Critics of labor unions view them as having a tendency to grab as much as they can in the short term, even if it means injuring workers in the long run by driving firms into bankruptcy or by blocking the new technologies and production methods that lead to economic growth. We will start with some facts about union membership in the United States.
p241.zh: 工会的主题可能会引起争议.工会的支持者将工会视为工人的主要防线,以抵御营利性企业压低工资和福利的努力。 对工会的批评者认为,他们往往在短期内尽可能地抓住,即使从长远来看这意味着通过推动企业破产或阻碍导致经济增长的新技术和生产方法而伤害工人。 我们首先要谈一下美国加入工会的一些事实。

p274.original: In terms of pay, benefits, and hiring, U.S. unions offer a good news/bad news story. The good news for unions and their members is that their members earn about 20% more than nonunion workers, even after adjusting for factors such as years of work experience and education level. The bad news for unions is that the share of U.S. workers who belong to a labor union has been steadily declining for 50 years, as  shows. About one-quarter of all U.S. workers belonged to a union in the mid-1950s, but only 10.3% of U.S. workers are union members today. If you leave out government workers (which includes teachers in public schools), only 6.1% of the workers employed by private firms now work for a union.
p274.zh: 在工资,福利,和雇佣方面,美国工会提供了一个好消息/坏消息.工会及其会员的好消息是,工会会员的收入比非工会工人高出约20%,即使在适应了工作经验和教育水平等因素之后也是如此。工会的坏消息是,50年来,加入工会的美国工人的比例一直在稳步下降,如上所示.大约四分之一的美国工人在1950年代中期属于一个工会,但今天只有10.3%的美国工人是工会会员. 如果将政府工作人员(包括公立学校的教师)排除在外,私人企业雇用的工人中只有6.1%现在为工会工作。

p275.original: Percentage of Wage and Salary Workers Who Are Union Members
p275.zh: 参加工会的工薪工人百分比

p276.original: The following section analyzes the higher pay union workers receive compared the pay rates for nonunion workers. The section after that analyzes declining union membership levels. An overview of these two issues will allow us to discuss many aspects of how unions work.
p276.zh: 下节分析了工会工人领取的工资高于非工会工人的工资标准。之后的一节分析了工会会员人数不断下降的情况。 对这两个问题的概述将使我们能够讨论工会如何运作的诸多方面。

p278.original: How does a union affect wages and employment?  Because a union is the sole supplier of labor, it can act like a monopoly and ask for whatever wage rate it can obtain for its workers.  If employers need workers, they have to meet the union’s wage demand.
p278.zh: 工会如何影响工资和就业? 由于工会是唯一的劳动力供应者,它可以像垄断一样采取行动,要求为其工人获得任何工资。 如果雇主需要工人,他们必须满足工会的工资需求。

p279.original: What are the limits on how much higher pay union workers can receive? To analyze these questions, let’s consider a situation where all firms in an industry must negotiate with a single union, and no firm is allowed to hire nonunion labor. If no labor union existed in this market, then equilibrium (E) in the labor market would occur at the intersection of the demand for labor (D) and the supply of labor (S) as we see in .  This is the same result as we showed in Figure 14.6 above.  The union can, however, threaten that, unless firms agree to the wages they demand, the workers will strike. As a result, the labor union manages to achieve, through negotiations with the firms, a union wage of Wu for its members, above what the equilibrium wage would otherwise have been.
p279.zh: 工会工人可领取多少高工资的限制是什么? 为了分析这些问题,让我们来考虑一个行业中的所有企业都必须与单一的工会谈判,不允许任何企业雇用非工会劳工的情况。 如果这个市场不存在工会,那么劳动力市场的平衡(E)就会发生在劳动力需求(D)和劳动力供应(S)的交汇点上,正如我们所看到的。 这与上文图14.6所示的结果相同。 但是,工会可能威胁说,除非企业同意他们所要求的工资,否则工人将罢工。 因此,工会设法通过与企业谈判,为其成员争取到吴的工会工资,其工资要高于本来会达到的平衡工资。

p281.original: This labor market situation resembles what a monopoly firm does in selling a product, but in this case a union is a monopoly selling labor to firms. At the higher union wage Wu, the firms in this industry will hire less labor than they would have hired in equilibrium. Moreover, an excess supply of workers want union jobs, but firms will not be hiring for such jobs.
p281.zh: 这种劳动力市场情况类似于垄断公司出售产品的做法,但在这种情况下,工会是向公司出售劳动力的垄断。 如果工会给吴工资较高,这个行业的公司将雇用的劳动力将少于平衡时雇用的劳动力。 此外,过多的工人需要工会工作,但公司不会雇用他们从事这种工作。

p282.original: From the union point of view, workers who receive higher wages are better off. However, notice that the quantity of workers (Qd) hired at the union wage Wu is smaller than the quantity Qe that the firm would have hired at the original equilibrium wage. A sensible union must recognize that when it pushes up the wage, it also reduces the firms’ incentive to hire. This situation does not necessarily mean that union workers are fired. Instead, it may be that when union workers move on to other jobs or retire, they are not always replaced, or perhaps when a firm expands production, it expands employment somewhat less with a higher union wage than it would have done with the lower equilibrium wage. Other situations could be that a firm decides to purchase inputs from nonunion producers, rather than producing them with its own highly paid unionized workers, or perhaps the firm moves or opens a new facility in a state or country where unions are less powerful.
p282.zh: 从工会的角度来看,工资较高的工人生活比较好. 然而,注意到工会雇用的工人(Qd)工资低于企业按原平衡工资雇用的Qe。明智的工会必须认识到,当它提高工资时,它也会减少企业的雇佣动机。 这种情况并不一定意味着工会工人被解雇。 相反,当工会工人转向其他工作或退休时,他们并不总是被取代,或者当一家企业扩大生产时,它以比低的平衡工资略低的工会工资来扩大就业。 其他情况可能是,一家公司决定从非工会生产商购买投入,而不是用自己的高薪工会工人生产投入,或者,一家公司可能在工会力量较小的国家或国家移动或开设新的设施。

p283.original: From the firm’s point of view, the key question is whether union workers’ higher wages are matched by higher productivity. If so, then the firm can afford to pay the higher union wages and, the demand curve for “unionized” labor could actually shift to the right. This could reduce the job losses as the equilibrium employment level shifts to the right and the difference between the equilibrium and the union wages will have been reduced. If worker unionization does not increase productivity, then the higher union wage will cause lower profits or losses for the firm.
p283.zh: 从公司的角度来看,关键问题是工会工人的较高工资是否与更高的生产率相匹配。 如果是这样,那么公司可以支付较高的工会工资,而“工会化”劳动力的需求曲线实际上可以转向右翼。 随着就业平衡水平向右转移,而且平衡与工会工资之间的差别将缩小,这可以减少失业。 如果工人工会化不能提高生产力,那么较高的工会工资将给企业带来较低的利润或损失.

p284.original: Union workers might have higher productivity than nonunion workers for a number of reasons. First, higher wages may elicit higher productivity. Second, union workers tend to stay longer at a given job, a trend that reduces the employer’s costs for training and hiring and results in workers with more years of experience. Many unions also offer job training and apprenticeship programs.
p284.zh: 由于一些原因,工会工人的生产率可能高于非工会工人。 首先,工资的提高可能带来更高的生产率。 第二,工会工人往往在某项工作上停留更长的时间,这一趋势降低了雇主的培训和雇用费用,并导致拥有更多年经验的工人。 许多工会还提供职业培训和学徒方案。

p285.original: In addition, firms that are confronted with union demands for higher wages may choose production methods that involve more physical capital and less labor, resulting in increased labor productivity.  provides an example. Assume that a firm can produce a home exercise cycle with three different combinations of labor and manufacturing equipment. Say that the firm pays labor $16 an hour (including benefits) and the machines for manufacturing cost $200 each. Under these circumstances, the total cost of producing a home exercise cycle will be lowest if the firm adopts the plan of 50 hours of labor and one machine, as the table shows. Now, suppose that a union negotiates a wage of $20 an hour including benefits. In this case, it makes no difference to the firm whether it uses more hours of labor and fewer machines or less labor and more machines, although it might prefer to use more machines and to hire fewer union workers. (After all, machines never threaten to strike—but they do not buy the final product or service either.)
p285.zh: 此外,面临工会要求提高工资的企业可能选择涉及更多有形资本和较少劳动力的生产方法,从而导致劳动生产率的提高。假设一家公司可以生产一个家庭运动周期,其劳动和制造设备有三种不同的组合。说公司支付每小时16美元的劳动力(包括福利),制造机器每台花费200美元. 在这种情况下,如上表所示,如果企业采用50小时劳动和一台机器的计划,生产家庭锻炼周期的总成本将是最低的。 现在,假设一个工会谈判一个每小时20美元的工资,包括福利。 在这种情况下,它是否使用更多的工时和较少的机器和更多的机器,对公司没有区别,尽管它可能更喜欢使用更多的机器和雇用较少的工会工人.(毕竟,机器从不威胁要罢工,但他们也不购买最终产品或服务。 )

p286.original: In the final column of the table, the wage has risen to $24 an hour. In this case, the firm clearly has an incentive for using the plan that involves paying for fewer hours of labor and using three machines. If management responds to union demands for higher wages by investing more in machinery, then union workers can be more productive because they are working with more or better physical capital equipment than the typical nonunion worker. However, the firm will need to hire fewer workers.
p286.zh: 在表最后一栏,工资已增至每小时24美元。 在这种情况下,公司显然有利用计划的积极性,该计划涉及支付更少的劳动小时和使用三台机器. 如果管理层通过对机械投资更多来响应工会对更高工资的要求,那么工会工人就可以更有生产力,因为他们使用比典型的非工会工人更多的或更好的实物资本设备工作. 然而,公司需要雇用较少的工人。

p308.original: In some cases, unions have discouraged the use of labor-saving physical capital equipment—out of the reasonable fear that new machinery will reduce the number of union jobs. For example, in 2015, the union representing longshoremen who unload ships and the firms that operate shipping companies and port facilities staged a work stoppage that shut down the ports on the western coast of the United States. Two key issues in the dispute were the desire of the shipping companies and port operators to use handheld scanners for record-keeping and computer-operated cabs for loading and unloading ships—changes which the union opposed, along with overtime pay. President Obama threatened to use the Labor Management Relations Act of 1947—commonly known as the Taft-Hartley Act—where a court can impose an 80-day “cooling-off period” in order to allow time for negotiations to proceed without the threat of a work stoppage. Federal mediators were called in, and the two sides agreed to a deal in February 2015. The ultimate agreement allowed the new technologies, but also kept wages, health, and pension benefits high for workers. In the past, presidential use of the Taft-Hartley Act sometimes has made labor negotiations more bitter and argumentative but, in this case, it seems to have smoothed the road to an agreement.
p308.zh: 在某些情况下,工会不鼓励使用节省劳力的实物资本设备,因为有理由担心新的机器会减少工会工作。 例如,2015年,代表卸船长岸人和经营航运公司和港口设施的公司的工会进行了停工,关闭了美国西海岸的港口。争议的两个关键问题是航运公司和港口经营人希望使用手持扫描仪进行记录保存,并使用计算机操作的驾驶室进行船舶装卸,工会反对这些更改以及加班费。奥巴马总统威胁说,要使用1947年的《劳动管理关系法》——通常称为《塔夫特-哈特利法》——法院可以规定80天的“冷却期”,以便有时间在不受到停工威胁的情况下进行谈判。联邦调解员被召来,双方于2015年2月达成协议.最终协议允许采用新技术,但也使工人的工资、健康和养恤金福利保持较高水平。 过去,总统使用塔夫特-哈特利法案有时使劳工谈判更加苦恼和争辩,但在这种情况下,它似乎为达成协议铺平了道路。

p309.original: In other instances, unions have proved quite willing to adopt new technologies. In one prominent example, during the 1950s and 1960s, the United Mineworkers union demanded that mining companies install labor-saving machinery in the mines. The mineworkers’ union realized that over time, the new machines would reduce the number of jobs in the mines, but the union leaders also knew that the mine owners would have to pay higher wages if the workers became more productive, and mechanization was a necessary step toward greater productivity.
p309.zh: 在其他情况下,工会证明非常愿意采用新技术。 一个突出的例子就是,在1950年代和1960年代,联合矿业工人联盟要求采矿公司在矿场安装节省劳力的机械。矿工工会意识到,随着时间的推移,新的机器会减少矿工的数量,但工会领导人也知道,如果矿工产量提高,矿工业主必须支付更高的工资,机械化是提高生产力的一个必要步骤。

p310.original: In fact, in some cases union workers may be more willing to accept new technology than nonunion workers, because the union workers believe that the union will negotiate to protect their jobs and wages, whereas nonunion workers may be more concerned that the new technology will replace their jobs. In addition, union workers, who typically have higher job market experience and training, are likely to suffer less and benefit more than non-union workers from the introduction of new technology. Overall, it is hard to make a definitive case that union workers as a group are always either more or less welcoming to new technology than are nonunion workers
p310.zh: 事实上,在某些情况下,工会工人可能比非工会工人更愿意接受新技术,因为工会工人相信工会会为保护自己的工作和工资进行谈判,而非工会工人可能更担心新技术会取代他们的工作. 此外,工会工人通常具有较高的就业市场经验和培训,他们可能比非工会工人少受苦,并从新技术的引进中获得更多好处。总体而言,很难确切证明工会工人作为一个群体,总是比非工会工人更或更少地欢迎新技术。

p311.original: The Decline in U.S. Union Membership

p312.original: The proportion of U.S. workers belonging to unions has declined dramatically since the early 1950s. Economists have offered a number of possible explanations:
p312.zh: 自1950年代初以来,美国工会工人的比例急剧下降。经济学家提出了若干可能的解释:

p313.original: The shift from manufacturing to service industries
p313.zh: 从制造业向服务业的转变

p314.original: The force of globalization and increased competition from foreign producers
p314.zh: 全球化的力量和外国生产者的竞争加剧

p315.original: A reduced desire for unions because of the workplace protection laws now in place
p315.zh: 由于现已制定工作场所保护法,减少对工会的渴望;

p316.original: U.S. legal environment that makes it relatively more difficult for unions to organize workers and expand their membership
p316.zh: 美国的法律环境使得工会组织工人和扩大其成员相对更加困难.

p317.original: Let’s discuss each of these four explanations in more detail.
p317.zh: 让我们更详细地讨论这四个解释中的每一个。

p318.original: A first possible explanation for the decline in the share of U.S. workers belonging to unions involves the patterns of job growth in the manufacturing and service sectors of the economy as  shows. The U.S. economy had about 15 million manufacturing jobs in 1960. This total rose to 19 million by the late 1970s and then declined to 17 million in 2013. Meanwhile, the number of jobs in service industries (including government employment) rose from 35 million in 1960 to over 118 million by 2013, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Because over time unions were stronger in manufacturing than in service industries, the growth in jobs was not happening where the unions were. It is interesting to note that government workers comprise several of the biggest unions in the country, including the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees (AFSCME); the Service Employees International Union; and the National Education Association.  lists the membership of each of these unions. Outside of government employees, however, unions have not had great success in organizing the service sector.
p318.zh: 工会会员中美国工人比例下降的第一个可能的解释是,正如所显示的那样,制造业和服务业的就业增长模式。1960年美国经济拥有约1500万个制造业就业岗位. 到1970年代后期,这一总数增加到1 900万,然后在2013年下降到1 700万。 同时,根据劳动统计局的统计,服务业(包括政府就业)的就业人数从1960年的3 500万增加到2013年的1.18亿以上。 由于随着时间的推移,工会在制造业比在服务业更强大,因此工会所在地的就业机会没有增长。令人感兴趣的是,政府工作人员是该国几个最大的工会,其中包括美国国家、县和市雇员联合会(AFSCME)、服务雇员国际联盟以及全国教育协会。 然而,在政府雇员之外,工会在组织服务部门方面没有取得很大成功。

p320.original: A second explanation for the decline in the share of unionized workers looks at import competition. Starting in the 1960s, U.S. carmakers and steelmakers faced increasing competition from Japanese and European manufacturers. As sales of imported cars and steel rose, the number of jobs in U.S. auto manufacturing fell. This industry is heavily unionized. Not surprisingly, membership in the United Auto Workers, which was 975,000 in 1985, had fallen to roughly 390,000 by 2015. Import competition not only decreases the employment in sectors where unions were once strong, but also decreases the bargaining power of unions in those sectors. However, as we have seen, unions that organize public-sector workers, who are not threatened by import competition, have continued to see growth.
p320.zh: 工会工人份额下降的第二个解释是,进口竞争。 从1960年代开始,美国汽车制造商和钢铁制造商面临着来自日本和欧洲制造商的日益激烈的竞争. 随着进口汽车和钢铁的销售额上升,美国汽车制造业的工作岗位数量下降. 这个行业的工会化程度很高.毫不奇怪,1985年联合汽车工人联盟的会员人数为97.5万人,到2015年已降至约39万人。进口竞争不仅减少了工会一度很强大的部门的就业,而且削弱了这些部门的工会讨价还价的能力。 然而,正如我们所看到的那样,组织不受进口竞争威胁的公共部门工人的工会继续增长。

p321.original: A third possible reason for the decline in the number of union workers is that citizens often call on their elected representatives to pass laws concerning work conditions, overtime, parental leave, regulation of pensions, and other issues. Unions offered strong political support for these laws aimed at protecting workers but, in an ironic twist, the passage of those laws then made many workers feel less need for unions.
p321.zh: 工会工人人数减少的第三个可能原因是,公民经常要求其当选代表通过有关工作条件、加班、育儿假、养老金管理和其他问题的法律。工会对旨在保护工人的这些法律提供了强有力的政治支持,但具有讽刺意味的是,这些法律的通过使许多工人认为对工会的需求减少。

p322.original: These first three possible reasons for the decline of unions are all somewhat plausible, but they have a common problem. Most other developed economies have experienced similar economic and political trends, such as the shift from manufacturing to services, globalization, and increasing government social benefits and regulation of the workplace. Clearly there are cultural differences between countries as to their acceptance of unions in the workplace. The share of the population belonging to unions in other countries is very high compared with the share in the United States.  shows the proportion of workers in a number of the world’s high-income economies who belong to unions. The United States is near the bottom, along with France and Spain. The last column shows union coverage, defined as including those workers whose wages are determined by a union negotiation even if the workers do not officially belong to the union. In the United States, union membership is almost identical to union coverage. However, in many countries, the wages of many workers who do not officially belong to a union are still determined by collective bargaining between unions and firms.
p322.zh: 工会衰落的前三个可能的原因都有些合理,但它们有一个共同的问题。 其他大多数发达经济体也经历了类似的经济和政治趋势,例如从制造业转向服务业、全球化、政府社会福利增加和工作场所监管。很明显,各国在工作场所接受工会方面存在文化差异。与美国相比,其他国家的工会会员比例非常高。 这表明了世界一些高收入经济体中属于工会的工人比例。 美国与法国和西班牙一起接近底部. 最后一栏显示工会的覆盖范围,定义为包括那些工资由工会谈判决定的工人,即使这些工人并非正式属于工会。在美国,加入工会几乎与工会的覆盖范围相同. 然而,在许多国家,许多正式不属于工会的工人的工资仍然由工会和公司之间的集体谈判决定。

p353.original: These international differences in union membership suggest a fourth reason for the decline of union membership in the United States: perhaps U.S. laws are less friendly to the formation of unions than such laws in other countries. The close connection between union membership and a friendly legal environment is apparent in the history of U.S. unions. The great rise in union membership in the 1930s followed the passage of the National Labor Relations Act of 1935, which specified that workers had a right to organize unions and that management had to give them a fair chance to do so. The U.S. government strongly encouraged forming unions during the early 1940s in the belief that unions would help to coordinate the all-out production efforts needed during World War II. However, after World War II came the passage of the Taft-Hartley Act of 1947, which gave states the power to allow workers to opt out of the union in their workplace if they so desired. This law made the legal climate less encouraging to those seeking to form unions, and union membership levels soon started declining.
p353.zh: 这些工会会员的国际差异表明美国工会会员减少的第四个原因:也许美国法律对工会的组建不如其他国家的法律那么友好.加入工会与友好的法律环境之间的密切联系在美国工会历史上是显而易见的.1935年国家劳动关系法通过后,1930年代工会会员人数大增,该法规定工人有权组织工会,管理层必须给他们公平的机会来组织工会.美国政府在1940年代早期大力鼓励组建工会,认为工会将有助于协调二战期间所需的全方位生产努力. 然而,在二战之后,1947年的塔夫特-哈特利法案获得通过,该法案赋予了各州权力,允许工人在自己工作场所选择退出工会,如果他们愿意的话.这项法律使法律气氛对寻求组建工会的人不那么令人鼓舞,工会会员人数很快开始下降。

p354.original: The procedures for forming a union differ substantially from country to country. For example, the procedures in the United States and those in Canada are strikingly different. When a group of workers wishes to form a union in the United States, they announce this fact and set an election date when the firm's employees will vote in a secret ballot on whether to form a union. Supporters of the union lobby for a “yes” vote, and the firm's management lobbies for a “no” vote—often even hiring outside consultants for assistance in swaying workers to vote “no.” In Canada, by contrast, a union is formed when a sufficient proportion of workers (usually about 60%) signs an official card saying that they want a union. There is no separate “election date.” The management of Canadian firms is limited by law in its ability to lobby against the union. In addition, although it is illegal to discriminate and fire workers based on their union activity in the United States, the penalties are slight, making this a not so costly way of deterring union activity. In short, forming unions is easier in Canada—and in many other countries—than in the United States.
p354.zh: 组建工会的程序因国而异。 例如,美国和加拿大的程序大不相同。 当一群工人希望在美国组建工会时,他们宣布这一事实,并确定一个选举日期,即公司雇员将在关于是否组建工会的无记名投票中投票.工会游说团支持“赞成”投票,而企业管理层也支持“反对”投票 — — 甚至经常聘请外部顾问协助工人摇摆不定地投“反对 ” 。 相比之下,在加拿大,当足够比例的工人(通常约60%)在官方卡上签字表示他们想要工会时,工会就形成了。 没有单独的“选举日期”。 加拿大企业的管理受到法律的限制,因为其游说反对工会的能力受到限制。 此外,虽然在美国基于工会活动的歧视和解雇工人是非法的,但惩罚是轻而易举的,因此这不是一种如此昂贵的威慑工会活动的方法.简言之,在加拿大——以及在许多其他国家——组建工会比在美国更容易。

p355.original: In summary, union membership in the United States is lower than in many other high-income countries, a difference that may be due to different legal environments and cultural attitudes toward unions.
p355.zh: 总之,美国的工会会员人数低于其他许多高收入国家,这可能是由于法律环境和文化对工会的态度不同造成的。

p358.original:
A labor union is an organization of workers that negotiates as a group with employers over compensation and work conditions. Union workers in the United States are paid more on average than other workers with comparable education and experience. Thus, either union workers must be more productive to match this higher pay or the higher
pay will lead employers to find ways of hiring fewer union workers than they otherwise would. American union membership has been falling for decades. Some possible reasons include the shift of jobs to service industries; greater competition from globalization; the passage of worker-friendly legislation; and U.S. laws that are less favorable to organizing unions.
p358.zh: 工会是工人组成的组织,他们作为一个团体与雇主就报酬和工作条件进行谈判。在美国的工会工人的平均工资高于其他具有可比学历和经验的工人. 因此,工会工作者必须提高生产率,才能与这种高薪相匹配,或者工资的提高将促使雇主找到比他们本来会少雇用工会工人的办法。 美国工会会员数十年来一直在下降.某些可能的原因包括:将工作转向服务行业;全球化带来的更大竞争;通过了有利于工人的立法;美国的法律对组织工会不太有利。

p381.original: What happens when there is market power on both sides of the labor market, in other words, when a union meets a monopsony?  Economists call such a situation a bilateral monopoly.
p381.zh: 当劳动力市场的两边都有市场力量时,换句话说,当工会遇到垄断时,会发生什么?经济学家将这种情况称为双边垄断。

p383.original: is a combination of Figure 14.6 and Figure 14.11. A monopsony wants to reduce wages as well as employment, Wm and L* in the figure. A union wants to increase wages, but at the cost of lower employment, Wu and L* in the figure.  Since both sides want to reduce employment, we can be sure that the outcome will be lower employment compared to a competitive labor market.  What happens to the wage, though, is based on the monopsonist’s relative bargaining power compared to the bargaining power of the union.  The actual outcome is indeterminate in the graph, but it will be closer to Wu if the union has more power and closer to Wm if the monopsonist has more power.
p383.zh: 图14.6和图14.11的组合。 在数字中,一个垄断公司希望减少工资和就业,Wm和L*。工会希望增加工资,但以较低的就业成本为代价,在图中吴和L*. 由于双方都想减少就业,我们可以肯定,结果将会比竞争性劳动力市场更低。 但工资的下场在于独身主义者相对于工会的议价能力而言相对讨价还价的能力。实际结果在图中不确定,但如果工会拥有更多的权力,如果独身主义者拥有更多的权力,则会更接近吴.

p385.original: A bilateral monopoly is a labor market with a union on the supply side and a monopsony on the demand side.  Since both sides have monopoly power, the equilibrium level of employment will be lower than that for a competitive labor market, but the equilibrium wage could be higher or lower depending on which side negotiates better.  The union favors a higher wage, while the monopsony favors a lower wage, but the outcome is indeterminate in the model.
p385.zh: 双边垄断是供应方工会和需求方垄断的劳动力市场。 由于双方都拥有垄断权,就业平衡水平将低于竞争性劳动力市场的水平,但工资平衡水平可能更高或更低,这取决于哪一方谈判得更好。工会倾向于提高工资,而垄断则倾向于降低工资,但结果在模式中不确定。

p393.original: Barriers to equitable participation in the labor market drive down economic growth. When certain populations are underrepresented, underpaid, or mistreated in a labor market or industry, the negative outcomes can effect the larger economy. For example, many science and technology fields were either unwelcoming or overtly unaccepting of women and people of color. Some major contributors to these fields overcame these challenges. Mexican-American scientist Lydia Villa-Komaroff, for example, faced overt discrimination when her college advisor told her not to pursue chemistry because women didn't "belong" in chemistry. She pursued biology instead; she developed the first instance of synthetic insulin (the chemical that people with diabetes need in order to survive) through a process that has saved million of lives and is credited with launching the entire industry of biotechnology—one of the most important in the U.S. economy. But for every Villa-Komaroff, there have been thousands of women who were prevented from making those contributions. Beyond the personal impact on those people, consider the impact on those scientific fields, our overall quality of life, and the economy itself. Economist Lisa D. Cook has quantified the costs of these innovation losses. She estimates that GDP could be as much as 4.4% higher if women and people from minority populations were fully able to participate in the science and technology innovation process.
p393.zh: 阻碍公平参与劳动力市场的障碍驱使经济增长下滑。某些人口在劳动力市场或行业中代表性不足、薪酬低或受到虐待,其负面后果会影响到更大的经济。 例如,许多科学技术领域要么不受欢迎,要么公然不接受妇女和有色人种。这些领域的一些主要贡献者克服了这些挑战。 例如,墨西哥裔美国科学家莉迪亚·维拉-科马罗夫(Lydia Villa-Komaroff)在大学顾问告诉她不要追求化学时就面临公开的歧视,因为女性在化学中并不"属于". 她转而追求生物学;她通过挽救了数百万人的生命,并因启动整个生物技术产业——美国经济中最重要的产业之一——而发展了合成胰岛素(糖尿病患者生存所需的化学物质)的第一例. 但是,对于每个Villa-Komaroff,有数千名妇女被阻止作出这些贡献。 除了对这些人的个人影响之外,还要考虑对这些科学领域、我们总体生活质量以及经济本身的影响。经济学家丽莎·D.库克量化了这些创新损失的代价. 她估计,如果妇女和少数民族人口能够充分参与科技创新进程,国内生产总值可能高达4.4%。

p394.original: Discrimination involves acting on the belief that members of a certain group are inferior or deserve less solely because of a factor such as race, gender, or religion. There are many types of discrimination but the focus here will be on discrimination in labor markets, which arises if workers with the same skill levels—as measured by education, experience, and expertise—receive different pay or have different job opportunities because of their race or gender. Much of the data collected and published on these topics are limited in terms of the diversity of people represented, and focus particularly on binary gender, single-race, and single-ethnicity identities. While these characterizations do not capture the diversity of Americans, the findings are important in order to understand discrimination and other practices, and to consider the impacts of policies and changes. Also, while sex and gender are different, many data sets, laws, court decisions, and media accounts use the terms interchangeably. For consistency, we will use the terminology found in the source material and government data.
p394.zh: 歧视是指仅仅因为种族、性别或宗教等因素而认为某一群体的成员地位低下或理应更低。歧视有多种类型,但这里的重点是劳动力市场上的歧视,如果技能水平相同的工人——按教育、经验和专门知识衡量——因其种族或性别而获得不同的工资或不同的工作机会,就会产生这种歧视。收集和公布的关于这些专题的大部分数据在代表性人口的多样性方面是有限的,尤其侧重于二元性别、单一种族和单一族裔身份。 虽然这些定性没有体现美国人的多样性,但调查结果对于理解歧视和其他做法以及考虑政策和变化的影响十分重要。 此外,虽然性和性别不同,但许多数据集、法律、法院裁决和媒体账户可互换使用这些术语。 为了保持一致性,我们将使用来源材料和政府数据中的术语。

p395.original: Earnings Gaps by Race and Gender
p395.zh: 按种族和性别分列的收入差距

p396.original: A possible signal of labor market discrimination is when an employer pays one group less than another.  shows the average wage of Black workers as a ratio of the average wage of White workers and the average wage of female workers as a ratio of the average wage of male workers. Research by the economists Francine Blau and Laurence Kahn shows that the gap between the earnings of women and men did not move much in the 1970s, but has declined since the 1980s. Detailed analysis by economists Kerwin Kofi Charles and Patrick Bayer show that the gap between the earnings of Black and White people diminished in the 1970s, but grew again so that current differences are as wide as they were nearly 70 years ago. In both gender and race, an earnings gap remains.
p396.zh: 劳动力市场歧视的一个可能信号是,雇主付给一个群体的工资低于另一个群体。 这表明黑人工人的平均工资与白人工人的平均工资之比,以及女工的平均工资与男性工人的平均工资之比。经济学家弗朗辛·布劳(Francine Blau)和劳伦斯·卡恩(Laurence Kahn)的研究表明,男女收入的差距在1970年代没有多少变化,但自1980年代以来已经缩小.经济学家克尔温·科菲·查尔斯和帕特里克·拜尔的详细分析显示,黑白人的收入差距在1970年代有所缩小,但再次扩大,使得目前的差异与近70年前一样大. 在性别和种族方面,收入差距依然存在。

p397.original: Wage Ratios by Sex and Race
p397.zh: 按性别和种族分列的工资比率

p398.original: An earnings gap between average wages, in and of itself, does not prove that discrimination is occurring in the labor market. We need to apply the same productivity characteristics to all parties (employees) involved. Gender discrimination in the labor market occurs when employers pay people of a specific gender less despite those people having comparable levels of education, experience, and expertise. (Read the Clear It Up about the sex-discrimination suit brought against Walmart.) Similarly, racial discrimination in the labor market exists when employers pay racially diverse employees less than their coworkers of the majority race despite having comparable levels of education, experience, and expertise. To bring a successful gender discrimination lawsuit, an employee must prove the employer is paying them less than an employee of a different gender who holds a similar job, with similar educational attainment, and with similar expertise. Likewise, someone who wants to sue on the grounds of racial discrimination must prove that the employer pays them less than an employee of another race who holds a similar job, with similar educational attainment, and with similar expertise.
p398.zh: 平均工资之间的收入差距本身并不能证明劳动力市场上存在歧视。 我们需要对有关各方(雇员)适用同样的生产力特点。劳动力市场上的性别歧视发生在雇主向特定性别的人支付较少的报酬时,尽管这些人的教育、经验和专门知识水平相当。类似地,在劳动力市场上,尽管教育、经验和专门知识水平相当,但雇主向不同种族的雇员支付的工资却低于多数种族的同工,因此,在劳动力市场上也存在种族歧视。 为了成功提起性别歧视诉讼,雇员必须证明雇主付给他们的薪酬低于从事类似工作、具有类似教育程度和类似专业知识的不同性别的雇员。 同样,以种族歧视为由起诉的人必须证明,雇主付给他们的薪酬低于从事类似工作、具有类似教育程度和类似专门知识的另一种族的雇员。

p400.original: As stated previously and as we will see below, not every instance of a wage gap or employment inequity is a product of overt discrimination on the part of individual employers. Significant overall issues in societies, such as inequitable education or housing segregation, can lead to earning gaps and limitations on economic mobility. However, these wider issues usually affect people from minority populations and/or those who have been historically underrepresented in positions of power. Economist William A. Darity Jr., whose work is discussed in more detail below, indicates that individualized employer racism still exists, but it is largely practiced in "covert and subtle forms."
p400.zh: 如前所述,正如下文所述,并不是每个工资差距或就业不平等的事例都是个别雇主公开歧视的结果。社会上的重大整体问题,如教育不公平或住房隔离,可能导致收入差距和经济流动受到限制。 然而,这些更广泛的问题通常影响到少数群体人口和/或历史上担任权力职务人数不足的人。经济学家威廉·A. 小达利(Darity Jr.)的作品在下文有更详细的讨论,这表明个性化的雇主种族主义依然存在,但基本上以"隐蔽和微妙的形式"实施.

p401.original: What was the sex-discrimination case against Walmart?
p401.zh: 对沃尔玛的性别歧视案是什么?

p402.original: In one of the largest class-action sex-discrimination cases in U.S. history, 1.2 million female employees of Walmart claimed that the company engaged in wage and promotion discrimination. In 2011, the Supreme Court threw out the case on the grounds that the group was too large and too diverse to consider the case a class action suit. Lawyers for the women regrouped and were subsequently suing in smaller groups. Part of the difficulty for the female employees is that the court said that local managers made pay and promotion decisions that were not necessarily the company's policies as a whole. Consequently, female Walmart employees in Texas argued that their new suit would challenge the management of a “discrete group of regional district and store managers.” They claimed that these managers made biased pay and promotion decisions. However, in 2013, a federal district court rejected a smaller California class action suit against the company.
p402.zh: 在美国历史上最大的集体诉讼性别歧视案件中,沃尔玛公司120万女性雇员声称该公司从事工资和晋升歧视.2011年,最高法院以该团体太大,种类繁多为由将案件抛出,认为该案件是集体诉讼.妇女律师重新组合,随后被分成几个小组起诉。女性雇员面临的部分困难是,法院说,当地管理人员做出的工资和晋升决定不一定是公司整体政策。 因此,德克萨斯州的沃尔玛女雇员认为,她们的新诉讼将质疑“区域区和商店管理人员”的管理工作。 他们声称,这些管理人员做出有偏见的薪酬和晋升决定。 然而,2013年,一个联邦地区法院驳回了对该公司提出的一个较小的加利福尼亚州集体诉讼诉讼.

p403.original: On other issues, Walmart made the news again in 2013 when the National Labor Relations Board found Walmart guilty of illegally penalizing and firing workers who took part in labor protests and strikes. Walmart paid $11.7 million in back wages and compensation damages to women in Kentucky who were denied jobs due to their sex. And in 2020, a sex-based hiring discrimination lawsuit was filed by the U.S. Equal Employ­ment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), in which the EEOC alleged that Walmart conducted a physical ability test (known as the PAT) as a requirement for applicants to be hired as order fillers at Walmart’s grocery distribution centers nationwide, and that the PAT disproportionately excluded female applicants from jobs as grocery order fillers. In September 2020, Walmart and the EEOC agreed to a consent decree, which requires Walmart to cease all physical ability testing that had been used for purposes of hiring grocery distribution center order fillers. The decree also required Walmart to pay $20 million into a settlement fund to pay lost wages to women across the country who were denied grocery order filler positions because of the testing.
p403.zh: 在其他问题上,沃尔玛在2013年再次发布消息,当时国家劳资关系委员会认定沃尔玛非法惩罚和解雇了参加劳工抗议和罢工的工人.沃尔玛向肯塔基州因性别原因被拒绝工作的妇女支付了1,170万美元的背薪和赔偿损失.而在2020年,美国又提起了基于性别的雇佣歧视诉讼.平等就业机会委员会(EEOC)称,Walmart进行了体能测试(称为PAT),要求申请人被聘为Walmart全国杂货销售中心的订单填充员,而PAT不成比例地将女性申请人排除在杂货订单填充员之外。2020年9月,沃尔玛与平机会商定了一项同意令,要求沃尔玛停止所有用于雇佣杂货分销中心订单充值器的体能测试.该法令还要求沃尔马尔特向一个结算基金支付2 000万美元,以支付全国妇女的损失工资,这些妇女因测试而被拒绝提供杂货订单填补职位。

p404.zh: 调查女性/男性收入差距

p405.original: As a result of changes in law and culture, women began to enter the paid workforce in substantial numbers in the mid- to late-twentieth century. As of February 2022, 56.0% of women aged 20 and over held jobs, while 67.6% of men aged 20 and over did. Moreover, along with entering the workforce, women began to ratchet up their education levels. In 1971, 44% of undergraduate college degrees went to women. As of the 2018–19 academic year, women earned 57% of bachelor’s degrees. In 1970, women received 5.4% of the degrees from law schools and 8.4% of the degrees from medical schools. By 2017, women were receiving just over 50% of the law degrees, and by 2019, 48% of the medical degrees. There are now slightly more women than men in both law schools and medical schools. These gains in education and experience have reduced the female/male wage gap over time. However, concerns remain about the extent to which women have not yet assumed a substantial share of the positions at the top of the largest companies or in the U.S. Congress.
p405.zh: 由于法律和文化的改变,在20世纪中后期,妇女开始大量进入有薪劳动力队伍。 截至2022年2月,20岁及以上妇女有56.0%从事工作,20岁及以上男子有67.6%从事工作。 此外,随着妇女进入劳动力队伍,她们开始提高教育水平。1971年,44%的大学本科学位发给妇女。截止2018-19学年,女性获得57%的学士学位.1970年,妇女从法学院获得5.4%的学位,从医学院获得8.4%。 到2017年,女性获得法律学位的比例刚刚超过50%,到2019年,女性获得医学学位的比例达到48%. 现在,在法学院和医学院中,女性略多于男性。教育和经验方面的这些进步随着时间的推移减少了男女工资差距。 然而,妇女在多大程度上尚未在最大公司或美国占据相当大比例的职位,仍然令人关切。国会.

p406.original: There are factors that can lower women’s average wages. Women are likely to bear a disproportionately large share of household responsibilities. A mother of young children is more likely to drop out of the labor force for several years or work on a reduced schedule than is the father. As a result, women in their 30s and 40s are likely, on average, to have less job experience than men. In the United States, childless women with the same education and experience levels as men are typically paid comparably. However, women with families and children are typically paid about 7% to 14% less than other women of similar education and work experience. Meanwhile, married men earn about 10% to 15% more than single men with comparable education and work experience. This circumstance or practice is often referred to as the "motherhood penalty" and the "fatherhood bonus."
p406.zh: 有一些因素可以降低妇女的平均工资。妇女很可能承担不成比例的家庭责任。年幼子女的母亲比父亲更有可能在几年内退出劳动大军,或者在缩短的时间内工作。 因此,平均而言,30至40岁的妇女的工作经验可能比男子少。在美国,受教育程度和经验水平与男子相同的无子女妇女通常得到同等报酬。 然而,有家庭和子女的妇女的工资通常比其他受过类似教育和工作经验的妇女低7%至14%。 同时,已婚男子的收入比具有同等学历和工作经验的单身男子多10%至15%。 这种情节或做法常被称为"母亲惩罚"和"父亲奖励".

p407.original: Another aspect of the gender pay gap relates to work that isn’t actually paid, such as household chores, caring for children and other family members, and cooking. Studies have found that globally and within the United States, women undertake far more of this work than do men; even women who work full time and/or bring in the majority of family income take on more of this unpaid work than the men in their households.
p407.zh: 男女薪酬差距的另一个方面与实际没有报酬的工作有关,例如家务、照顾子女和其他家庭成员以及做饭。研究发现,在全球和美国,妇女从事的这种工作远远多于男子;即使是全职工作和(或)带来大部分家庭收入的妇女,从事这种无报酬工作的人数也比家庭中的男子多。

p408.original: Economists study many aspects of sex- and gender-based earnings gaps, often revealing unexpected causes and impacts. For example, economists Jessica Pan, Jonathan Guryan, and Kerwin Kofi Charles analyzed decades of sociological and employment data and uncovered that the amount of sexism in the U.S. state where a woman was born is an indicator of the woman's earnings throughout her life, even if she moves away from her home state. In other words, women born in states with more pronounced sexist attitudes earn less, no matter where they live later on. Other economists showed that from 1950–2000, as women's representation increased in the workforce, jobs that became occupied by women experienced wage reductions relative to jobs being done by men—an outcome often referred to as "devaluation." The value of this research and similar investigations comes from the deeper understanding of the origins of the earnings gap, so that workers, employers, and governments can take steps to address them.
p408.zh: 经济学家们研究了基于性和性别的收入差距的许多方面,常常揭示出出出意料的原因和影响。 例如,经济学家杰西卡·潘(Jessica Pan),乔纳森·古里安(Jonathan Guryan)和凯尔温·科菲·查尔斯(Kerwin Kofi Charles)分析了数十年的社会学和就业数据,并发现女性出生地美国州性别主义的数量是该女性一生收入的一个指标,即使她离开自己的家乡.换句话说,出生在性别歧视态度较明显的各州的妇女,无论她们后来生活在何处,收入都比较低。 其他经济学家则指出,1950-2000年,随着妇女在劳动力中的比例增加,妇女所从事工作的工资比男子所从事工作的工资有所下降——这一结果通常被称为“再评估 ” 。 这一研究和类似调查的价值来自对收入差距起源的更深入理解,这样工人、雇主和政府就可以采取措施解决这些问题。

p409.original: Visit this website to read more about the persistently low numbers of women in executive roles in business and in the U.S. Congress.
p409.zh: 访问该网站,了解妇女在企业和美国担任行政职务的人数持续偏低的情况。国会.

p410.original: Investigating the Earnings Gap Related to Race and Ethnicity
p410.zh: 调查与种族和族裔有关的收入差距

p411.original: Black people experienced blatant labor market discrimination during much of the twentieth century. Until the passage of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, it was legal in many states to refuse to hire a Black worker, regardless of the credentials or experience of that worker. Moreover, Black people were often denied access to educational opportunities, which in turn meant that they had lower levels of qualifications for many jobs. At least one economic study has shown that the 1964 law is partially responsible for the narrowing of the gap in Black–White earnings in the late 1960s and into the 1970s. For example, the ratio of total earnings of Black male workers to White male workers rose from 62% in 1964 to 75.3% in 2013, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
p411.zh: 在二十世纪的大部分时间里,黑人遭受了公然的劳动力市场歧视。 在1964年《民权法》通过之前,在许多州,拒绝雇用黑人工人是合法的,无论该工人的资格或经验如何。 此外,黑人往往得不到教育机会,这反过来意味着他们从事许多工作的资格水平较低。至少有一项经济研究表明,1964年的法律对缩小1960年代末和1970年代黑白收入差距负有部分责任。 例如,根据劳工统计局的数据,黑人男性工人与白人男性工人的总收入比率从1964年的62%上升到2013年的75.3%。

p412.original: However, the earnings gap between Black and White workers has not changed as much as the earnings gap between men and women has in the last half century. The remaining racial gap seems related both to continuing differences in education levels and to the presence of discrimination.  shows that the percentage of Black people who complete a four-year college degree remains substantially lower than the percentage of White people who complete college. According to the U.S. Census, both White and Black people have higher levels of educational attainment than Hispanic people and lower levels than Asian people. The lower average levels of education for Black workers surely explain part of the earnings gap. In fact, Black women who have the same levels of education and experience as White women receive, on average, about the same level of pay. One study shows that White and Black college graduates have identical salaries immediately after college; however, the racial wage gap widens over time, an outcome that suggests the possibility of continuing discrimination. Other researchers conducted a field experiment by responding to job advertisements with fictitious resumes using names that were either commonly associated with Black/African American people or names commonly associated with White people; they found that the White-associated names received 50 percent more callbacks for interviews. This is suggestive of discrimination in job opportunities. Further, as the following Clear It Up feature explains, there is evidence to support that discrimination in the housing market is connected to employment discrimination.
p412.zh: 然而,黑人和白人工人之间的收入差距并没有像过去半个世纪中男女之间的收入差距那样大的变化.剩下的种族差距似乎与教育程度的持续差异和歧视的存在有关。 这表明,完成四年大学学位的黑人的比例仍然大大低于完成大学学业的白人的比例。 据美国记载.人口普查显示,白人和黑人的受教育程度都高于西班牙人,低于亚洲人。黑人工人的平均教育水平较低,这无疑是收入差距的一部分。 事实上,与白人妇女具有同等教育程度和经验的黑人妇女平均得到的薪酬水平大致相同。一项研究表明,白人和黑人大学毕业生在大学毕业后立即获得同等工资;然而,种族工资差距随时间推移而扩大,这一结果表明有可能继续受到歧视。 其他研究者进行了实地试验,通过使用通常与黑人/非裔美国人有关的名字或与白人有关的名字的虚假简历来回应招聘广告;他们发现,与白人有关的名字在接受采访时多收到50%的回电。这表明在就业机会方面存在着歧视。 此外,正如以下 " Clear It Up " 特征所解释的,有证据表明,住房市场中的歧视与就业歧视有关。

p413.zh: 2019年按种族和族裔分列的18岁及以上个人受教育情况

p419.original: Completed four years of high school or more
p419.zh: 完成四年以上高中教育

p424.zh: 四年以上完成的大学教育

p429.original: How is discrimination in the housing market connected to employment discrimination?
p429.zh: 住房市场中的歧视与就业歧视有何关联?

p430.original: A recent study by the Housing and Urban Development (HUD) department found that realtors showed Black homebuyers 18 percent fewer homes compared to White homebuyers. Realtors showed Asian homebuyers 19 percent fewer properties. Additionally, Hispanic people experience more discrimination in renting apartments and undergo stiffer credit checks than White renters. In a 2012 study by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development and the nonprofit Urban Institute, Hispanic testers who contacted agents about advertised rental units received information about 12 percent fewer units available and were shown seven percent fewer units than White renters. The $9 million study, based on research in 28 metropolitan areas,  concluded that blatant “door slamming” forms of discrimination are on the decline but that the discrimination that does exist is harder to detect, and as a result, more difficult to remedy. According to the Chicago Tribune, HUD Secretary Shaun Donovan, who served in his role from 2009-2014, told reporters, “Just because it’s taken on a hidden form doesn’t make it any less harmful. You might not be able to move into that community with the good schools.”
p430.zh: 住房和城市发展部最近进行的一项研究发现,房地产经纪人显示,黑人购房人的住房比白人购房人少18%。房地产商显示亚洲购房商的房产减少了19%。 此外,西班牙裔人在出租公寓方面受到的歧视比白人的租户还要严重。 在2012年美国的一项研究中.住房和城市发展部以及非营利城市研究所,与代理商联系的西班牙裔测试人员获得的信息显示,可提供的租房单位比白人租房者少12%,而且显示的租房单位少7%。 根据对28个大都市地区的研究,900万美元的研究得出结论,公然的“敲门”歧视正在减少,但确实存在的歧视更难发现,因此更难补救。 根据《芝加哥论坛报》,2009-2014年任职的HUD秘书Shaun Donovan告诉记者说,“只是因为它是隐形的,不会减少它的危害。 你可能无法与好学校一起进入这个社区。”

p431.original: These practices are viewed as a continuation of redlining, which is the intentional and discriminatory withholding of services or products based on race or other factors. Redlining was practiced extensively by banks and other lenders who refused to issue mortgages or other loans to people from racial or ethnic minorities living in neighborhoods that were deemed "hazardous" to investment, even though the same lenders would issue loans to White people with similar economic status. Redlining has lasting effects today, demonstrated by significant divides in educational and financial opportunity in certain neighborhoods or cities.
p431.zh: 这些做法被视为继续重排,即基于种族或其他因素故意和歧视性地扣留服务或产品。银行和其他放款人广泛采用雷丁林的做法,他们拒绝向居住在被认为对投资“有害”的街区的种族或族裔少数群体的人发放抵押贷款或其他贷款,尽管同一放款人将向具有类似经济地位的白人发放贷款。某些社区或城市在教育和财政机会方面存在巨大差距,这表明今天重新调整调整具有持久影响。

p432.original: The lower levels of education for Black workers can also be a result of discrimination—although it may be pre-labor market discrimination, rather than direct discrimination by employers in the labor market. For example, if redlining and other discrimination in housing markets causes Black families to live clustered together in certain neighborhoods and those areas have under-resourced schools, then those children will continue to have lower educational attainment then their White counterparts and, consequently, not be able to obtain the higher paying jobs that require higher levels of education. Another element to consider is that in the past, when Black people were effectively barred from many high-paying jobs, obtaining additional education could have seemed not to be worth the investment, because the educational degrees would not pay off. While the government has legally abolished discriminatory labor practices, structures and systems take a very long time to eradicate.
p432.zh: 黑人工人受教育程度较低也可能是歧视的结果——尽管这可能是劳工前市场歧视,而不是劳动力市场上雇主的直接歧视。 例如,如果住房市场中的重新调整和其他歧视导致黑人家庭集中在某些街区,这些地区的学校资源不足,那么这些儿童的受教育程度就会继续较低,而白人则会下降,因此无法获得需要更高教育程度的高薪工作。 另一个需要考虑的因素是,在过去,当黑人被有效地禁止从事许多高薪工作时,获得更多的教育似乎并不值得投资,因为教育学位不会有所回报。 虽然政府在法律上废除了歧视性的劳动做法,但结构和制度需要很长的时间才能消除。

p434.original: Gary Becker (1930–2014), who won the Nobel Prize in economics in 1992, was one of the first to analyze discrimination in economic terms. Becker pointed out that while competitive markets can allow some employers to practice discrimination, it can also provide profit-seeking firms with incentives not to discriminate. Given these incentives, Becker explored the question of why discrimination persists.
p434.zh: 1992年获得诺贝尔经济学奖的加里·贝克尔(1930–2014)是最早分析经济方面歧视的人物之一.Becker指出,虽然竞争性市场可以允许一些雇主实行歧视,但也可以为寻求利润的公司提供不歧视的奖励。 鉴于这些激励措施,贝克尔探讨了为什么歧视继续存在的问题。

p435.original: If a business is located in an area with a large minority population and refuses to sell to minorities, it will cut into its own profits. If some businesses run by bigoted employers refuse to pay women and/or minorities a wage based on their productivity, then other profit-seeking employers can hire these workers. In a competitive market, if the business owners care more about the color of money than about the color of skin, they will have an incentive to make buying, selling, hiring, and promotion decisions strictly based on economic factors.
p435.zh: 企业位于少数民族人口较多的地区,拒绝向少数民族出售的,将自谋利. 如果一些雇主偏执经营的企业拒绝根据她们的生产力向妇女和/或少数民族支付工资,那么其他寻求利润的雇主可以雇用这些工人。 在竞争性市场中,如果企业主更关心金钱的颜色而不是皮肤的颜色,那么他们就会有动机严格根据经济因素做出买卖,雇用和晋升决定.

p436.original: Do not underestimate the power of markets to offer at least a degree of freedom to oppressed groups. In many countries, cohesive minority population groups like Jewish people and emigrant Chinese people have managed to carve out a space for themselves through their economic activities, despite legal and social discrimination against them. Many immigrants, including those who come to the United States, have taken advantage of economic freedom to make new lives for themselves. However, history teaches that market forces alone are unlikely to eliminate discrimination. After all, discrimination against African Americans persisted in the market-oriented U.S. economy during the century between the ratification of the 13th Amendment, which abolished slavery in 1865, and the passage of the Civil Rights Act of 1964—and has continued since then, too.
p436.zh: 不要低估市场至少向被压迫群体提供某种程度自由的力量。在许多国家,有凝聚力的少数民族群体,如犹太人和移民的中国人,尽管在法律上和社会上对他们有歧视,却通过经济活动为自己开辟了空间。 许多移民,包括来美国的人,都利用经济自由为自己创造新生活. 然而,历史表明,单靠市场力量不可能消除歧视。毕竟,从1865年批准废除奴隶制的第十三修正案到1964年《民权法》的通过,美国经济在以市场为导向的过程中一直存在对非裔美国人的歧视,而且从那时起,这种歧视也一直在持续。

p437.original: Why does discrimination persist in competitive markets? Gary Becker sought to explain this persistence. Discriminatory impulses can emerge at a number of levels: among managers, among workers, and among customers. Consider the situation of a store owner or manager who is not personally prejudiced, but who has many customers who are prejudiced. If that manager treats all groups fairly, the manager may find it drives away prejudiced customers. In such a situation, a policy of nondiscrimination could reduce the firm’s profits. After all, a business firm is part of society, and a firm that does not follow the societal norms is likely to suffer.
p437.zh: 为什么在竞争性市场上歧视继续存在?盖瑞·贝克尔试图解释这种持久性.歧视的冲动可能在若干层面出现:管理人员、工人和顾客。考虑一下店主或经理的情况,他们虽然没有个人偏见,但有许多顾客受到偏见. 如果这位经理公平对待所有团体,经理可能会发现这驱使了偏见的顾客. 在这种情况下,不歧视政策可减少公司的利润。毕竟,一个企业是社会的一部分,一个不遵守社会规范的企业很可能遭受损失。

p438.original: As economist William A. Darity Jr. points out, however, the "prejudiced customer" rationale falls apart when considering the many jobs that have no customer contact. Darity examined several theories regarding the persistence of employment discrimination, including rationales regarding group membership and employers' lack of information about candidates of other genders or races. Darity also directly studies and interprets others' work on discrimination in other countries, such as wage disparities between Sikh and Hindu men in India. Darity concludes that the competitive forces of the market have not been enough to overcome employment and wage discrimination, and, on their own, are unlikely to end such discrimination in the future.
p438.zh: 作为经济学家威廉·A. 然而,Darity Jr.指出,在考虑许多没有客户接触的工作时,"受损害的客户"的原理会分崩离析.Darity研究了有关就业歧视持续存在的若干理论,包括关于群体成员资格和雇主缺乏其他性别或种族候选人信息的理由。达利蒂还直接研究并解释其他国家的歧视工作,如印度锡克教和印度教男子之间的工资差距.Darity的结论是,市场的竞争力量不足以克服就业和工资歧视,而且单靠自身力量不可能在今后结束这种歧视。

p439.original: Read this article to learn more about wage discrimination.
p439.zh: 阅读此条,以了解更多有关工资歧视的情况。

p441.original: A first public policy step against discrimination in the labor market is to make it illegal. For example, the Equal Pay Act of 1963 said that employers must pay men and women who do equal work the same. The Civil Rights Act of 1964 prohibits employment discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin. The Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967 prohibited discrimination on the basis of age against individuals who are 40 years of age or older. The Civil Rights Act of 1991 provides monetary damages in cases of intentional employment discrimination. The Pregnancy Discrimination Act of 1978 was aimed at prohibiting discrimination against people in the workplace who are planning pregnancy, are pregnant, or are returning after pregnancy. Passing a law, however, is only part of the answer, since discrimination by prejudiced employers may be less important than broader social patterns and systems.
p441.zh: 打击劳动力市场歧视的第一个公共政策步骤是将其定为非法。 例如,1963年《同酬法》规定,雇主必须向从事同样工作的男子和妇女支付同等报酬。1964年《公民权利法》禁止基于种族、肤色、宗教、性别或民族血统的就业歧视。1967年《就业年龄歧视法》禁止对40岁或以上个人基于年龄的歧视。1991年的《民权法》规定了故意就业歧视案件中的金钱赔偿。1978年的《怀孕歧视法》旨在禁止在工作场所歧视计划怀孕、怀孕或怀孕后返回的人。 然而,通过法律只是答案的一部分,因为偏见雇主的歧视可能不如更广泛的社会模式和制度重要。

p442.original: The 1964 Civil Rights Act created an important government organization, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, to investigate employment discrimination and protect workers who filed complaints against employers. Economist Phyllis Ann Wallace, who had previously worked for U.S. intelligence services, was appointed as the commission's chief of technical studies. In this role she collected and organized a massive amount of public and private sector data, as well as mentored and directed economists and other analysts in their investigations.
p442.zh: 1964年《公民权利法》建立了一个重要的政府组织,即平等就业机会委员会,调查就业歧视,保护对雇主提出申诉的工人。此前在美国情报部门工作的经济学家菲利斯·安·华莱士(Phyllis Ann Wallace)被任命为委员会的技术研究主任. 在这一作用中,她收集并组织了大量公共和私营部门的数据,指导和指导经济学家和其他分析人员进行调查。

p443.original: These laws against discrimination have reduced the gender wage gap. A 2007 Department of Labor study compared salaries of men and women who have similar educational achievement, work experience, and occupation and found that the gender wage gap is only 5%.
p443.zh: 这些反歧视法律缩小了男女工资差距。劳工部2007年的一项研究比较了具有类似教育成就、工作经验和职业的男女工资,发现男女工资差距仅为5%。

p444.original: In the case of the earnings gap between Black people and White people (and also between Hispanic people and White people), probably the single largest step that could be taken at this point in U.S. history to close the earnings gap would be to reduce the gap in educational attainment. Part of the answer to this issue involves finding ways to improve the performance of schools, which is a highly controversial topic in itself. In addition, the education gap is unlikely to close unless Black and Hispanic families and peer groups strengthen their culture of support for educational attainment.
p444.zh: 就黑人和白人(以及西班牙人和白人)之间的收入差距而言,在美国历史上目前可以采取的缩小收入差距的最大步骤可能是缩小受教育程度的差距。对这一问题的部分答案是寻找方法来提高学校的成绩,这本身就是一个极具争议性的主题. 此外,除非黑人和西班牙裔家庭及同龄人加强支持受教育的文化,否则教育差距就不可能缩小。

p445.original: Affirmative action is the name given to active efforts by government or businesses that give special rights to minorities in hiring and promotion to make up for past discrimination. Affirmative action, in its limited and not especially controversial form, means making an effort to reach out to a broader range of minority candidates for jobs. In its more aggressive and controversial form, affirmative action required government and companies to hire a specific number or percentage of minority employees. However, the U.S. Supreme Court has ruled against state affirmative action laws. Today, the government applies affirmative action policies only to federal contractors who have lost a discrimination lawsuit. The federal Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) enforces this type of redress.
p445.zh: 平权行动是政府或企业在雇用和晋升方面给予少数群体特殊权利的积极努力的名称,以弥补过去的歧视。平权行动,其形式有限,并不特别有争议,意味着努力接触更广泛的少数群体候选人。平权行动以更具侵略性和争议性的形式,要求政府和公司雇用一定数量或百分比的少数群体雇员。 然而,美国.最高法院裁定州级平权行动法无效. 今天,政府只对失去歧视诉讼的联邦承包商适用平权行动政策。联邦平等就业机会委员会(EEOC)负责实施这类补救。

p446.zh: 日益多样化的劳动力队伍

p447.original: Racial and ethnic diversity is on the rise in the U.S. population and workforce. As  shows, while the White Americans comprised 78% of the population in 2012, the U.S. Bureau of the Census projects that Whites will comprise 69% of the U.S. population by 2060. Forecasters predict that the proportion of U.S. citizens who are of Hispanic background to rise substantially. Moreover, in addition to expected changes in the population, workforce diversity is increasing as the women who entered the workforce in the 1970s and 1980s are now moving up the promotion ladders within their organizations.
p447.zh: 种族和族裔多样性在美国人口和劳动力中呈上升趋势. 如前所述,2012年美国白人人口占总人口的78%,而美国则占总人口的78%。人口普查局预计,到2060年,白人将占美国人口的69%.预测者预测,具有西班牙背景的美国公民比例会大幅上升. 此外,除了预期的人口变化之外,随着1970年代和1980年代进入劳动力队伍的妇女正在其组织内晋升阶梯的上升,劳动力的多样性也在增加。

p448.original: Projected Changes in America’s Racial and Ethnic Diversity
p448.zh: 美国种族和族裔多样性的预期变化

p449.original: Regarding the future, optimists argue that the growing proportions of minority workers will break down remaining discriminatory barriers. The economy will benefit as an increasing proportion of workers from traditionally disadvantaged groups have a greater opportunity to fulfill their potential. Pessimists worry that the social tensions between different genders and between ethnic groups will rise and that workers will be less productive as a result. Anti-discrimination policy, at its best, seeks to help society move toward the more optimistic outcome.
p449.zh: 关于未来,乐观主义者认为,少数群体工人比例的不断上升将打破仍然存在的歧视性障碍。经济将受益,因为来自传统弱势群体的工人中,有更大的机会实现其潜力。悲观主义者担心不同性别之间和不同种族群体之间的社会紧张关系会上升,因此工人的生产力会因此降低.反歧视政策最多只能帮助社会走向更乐观的结果。

p450.original: The FRED database includes data on foreign and native born civilian population  and labor force.
p450.zh: FRED数据库包括外国和本地出生的平民人口和劳动力数据。

p452.original:
Discrimination occurs in a labor market when employers pay workers with the same economic characteristics, such as education, experience, and skill, are paid different amounts because of race, gender, religion, age, or disability status. In the
United States, female workers on average earn less than male workers, and Black workers on average earn less than White workers. There is controversy over to which discrimination
differences in factors like education and job experience can explain these earnings gaps. Free markets can allow discrimination to occur, but the threat of a loss of sales or a loss of productive workers can also create incentives for a firm not to discriminate.
A range of public policies can be used to reduce earnings gaps between men and women or between White and other
racial/ethnic groups: requiring equal pay for equal work, and attaining more equal educational outcomes.
p452.zh: 在劳动力市场上,当雇主向具有相同经济特征的工人支付工资时,例如教育、经验和技能,则因种族、性别、宗教、年龄或残疾状况而得到不同数额的工资。在美国,女性工人的平均收入低于男性工人,黑人工人的平均收入低于白人工人. 对于教育和工作经验等因素中的歧视差异能解释这些收入差距,存在争议。自由市场可以允许发生歧视,但失去销售或生产性工人的威胁也可促使企业不歧视。可以利用一系列公共政策来缩小男女或白人与其他种族/族裔群体之间的收入差距:要求同工同酬,并取得更平等的教育成果。
